Ratio Analysis: Formulas, Examples and How to Interpret Them

Ratios turn the numbers in financial statements into comparisons that mean something. This guide gives the main formulas by category, all worked on the same company, and shows how to read them.

2 min readFor MBA, BBA and BBMUpdated 2 November 2026

The figures used

All examples use Sunrise Traders Ltd from our balance sheet and profit and loss guides (₹ lakh): revenue 1,000; COGS 600; EBIT 200; interest 40; PAT 120; current assets 300; inventory 120; receivables 100; current liabilities 200; total debt 350; long-term debt 300; equity 400; total assets 900.

Liquidity ratios: can it pay its short-term bills?

RatioFormulaResult
Current ratioCurrent assets ÷ current liabilities300 ÷ 200 = 1.5
Quick ratio(Current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities180 ÷ 200 = 0.9

Solvency ratios: can it carry its debt?

RatioFormulaResult
Debt-to-equityTotal debt ÷ equity350 ÷ 400 = 0.875
Interest coverageEBIT ÷ interest200 ÷ 40 = 5 times

Profitability ratios: how much does it earn?

RatioFormulaResult
Gross marginGross profit ÷ revenue400 ÷ 1,000 = 40%
Net marginPAT ÷ revenue120 ÷ 1,000 = 12%
ROEPAT ÷ equity120 ÷ 400 = 30%
ROCEEBIT ÷ (equity + long-term debt)200 ÷ 700 = 28.6%

Efficiency ratios: how well does it use its assets?

RatioFormulaResult
Asset turnoverRevenue ÷ total assets1,000 ÷ 900 = 1.11 times
Inventory turnoverCOGS ÷ inventory600 ÷ 120 = 5 times
Debtor daysReceivables ÷ revenue × 365100 ÷ 1,000 × 365 = 36.5 days

Valuation ratios: what is the market paying?

  • P/E ratio: share price ÷ EPS. At a price of ₹180 and EPS of ₹12, the P/E is 15.
  • P/B: share price ÷ book value per share. At ₹180 and book value of ₹40, it is 4.5.
  • Dividend yield: dividend per share ÷ share price.
  • EV/EBITDA: enterprise value ÷ EBITDA, which is neutral to how much debt a company has.

DuPont analysis: what drives ROE

ROE = net margin × asset turnover × equity multiplier = 12% × 1.11 × (900 ÷ 400 = 2.25) = 30%.

DuPont shows whether a high ROE comes from strong margins, efficient use of assets, or simply heavy debt. Two companies can have the same ROE for very different reasons, and the one relying on debt carries more risk.

Limits of ratio analysis

  • Book values are based on historical cost, and ignore inflation.
  • Different accounting policies make comparison harder.
  • A ratio shows one date, which may be flattered by year-end window dressing.
  • A ratio means little alone: compare over time and with peers in the same industry.

Exam and interview questions

What is an ideal current ratio?

The textbook answer is 2:1, and for the quick ratio 1:1, but what is normal varies by industry. Retailers with fast cash collection can run comfortably below 1.

What is the difference between ROE and ROCE?

ROE measures return on shareholders' money only. ROCE measures return on all long-term funds, so it also shows how well the company earns on borrowed money, and is more useful for comparing firms with different levels of debt.

What are the main types of ratios?

Liquidity, solvency, profitability, efficiency (turnover) and valuation or market ratios.
